message:
Now I understand the path. When a string like `"-999999999999999999999999999999"` (a negative number too big for a fixnum) is converted to an integer, it goes through `mrb_bint_new_str` with `p2` pointing to the string (including the `-` sign) and `p3-p2` as the length. Then in `mpz_init_set_str`, when it sees `-`, it does `s++` but doesn't decrement `len`, causing an out-of-bounds read.

Let me check the fuzzer harness to understand what input format is expected:

<｜｜DSML｜｜=execute_bash>
<parameter=command>ls /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/oss-fuzz/ && cat /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/oss-fuzz/*.c 2>/dev/null | head -100</｜｜DSML｜｜>
</｜｜DSML｜｜>
